sections.voiceover: What happens when 17,700 cubic metres per second surge over Iguazu Falls?
b_roll: Aerial view of Iguazu Falls during high water flow
Map highlighting the border between Argentina and Brazil

sections.voiceover: In October 2026, a super El Nino weather pattern delivered heavy rainfall across South America. Why did heavy rain cause Rio Iguazu to flow at six times the normal rate?
b_roll: Satellite imagery of South America showing weather patterns
Raging river waters near Iguazu National Park

text_overlay.text: Super El Nino floods Rio Iguazu

sections.voiceover: However, that massive surge sent twelve times the average flow across Argentina and Brazil.
b_roll: Graph showing water flow multiplication compared to average

sections.voiceover: Iguazu Falls spans more than a mile, featuring a complex experiencing 17,700 cubic metres per second.
b_roll: Wide shot of Iguazu Falls spanning Argentina and Brazil
Closed gates at Circuito Superior walkway

sections.voiceover: Iguazu National Park officials temporarily restricted tourist access.
